key_insight: A measurement-free protocol corrects single-photon loss in a superconducting cavity and extends simulated logical-qubit lifetime beyond an unprotected encoding.
engineering_relevance: Coherent, cavity-level error correction could reduce the error burden on an outer quantum error-correcting code without requiring syndrome measurements.
method: Encode a logical qubit in one cavity using the lowest-order binomial code.
Use two ancillary cavities and Josephson-junction-based nonlinear couplings for coherent error correction.
Optimize the waiting time between correction rounds.
evidence_signal: Numerical simulations with experimentally realistic parameters show 99% single-photon-loss correction fidelity and a 1.2–1.8× logical-lifetime gain over an unprotected Fock {|0⟩, |1⟩} encoding.
watch_item: The reported gains are simulation-based; experimental performance must be validated under hardware imperfections.
paper_title: A measurement-free quantum error correction protocol for superconducting cavities
